column5: Every ruler adds to this castle in their own way.\nI've been in power for several decades by now.\nYou're the only one who's ever noticed my addition.
column6: 每位统治者都会以自己的方式为这座城堡添砖加瓦。\n我掌权至今已有数十年。\n你是唯一一个注意到我这份添置的人。

column5: You made it that way!?\nDoes that mean you like to climb, too?
column6: 那是你弄的！？\n这么说你也喜欢攀爬？

column5: Yes, it does. \nThat's how I start my day.\nThere's no workout quite like it.
column6: 没错。\n我每天都这样开始新的一天。\n没有什么锻炼比得上它。

column5: Do you use any special equipment?\nI got some metallic claw-like things in Mazeo.
column6: 你用专门的装备吗？\n我在马泽奥弄到了一些金属爪一样的东西。

column5: I have no use for such things.\nI prefer to go it alone, without safety.\nIt makes you think about every little move.
column6: 那种东西我用不上。\n我更喜欢独自上阵，不用任何保护。\n这样你才会认真思考每一个动作。

column5: One accident, and you fall to your death.\nYou don't need those claws. Just climb smarter.\nA handicap takes away your sense of achievement.
column6: 一次失手，你就会摔下去送命。\n你不需要那些爪子。爬得聪明点就行。\n借助外物会夺走你的成就感。

column5: I think I'll need them, actually.\nI'm planning to climb The Grand Tree in Valinorth.\nIf you saw it, you'd understand the necessity.
column6: 其实我觉得我会需要它们。\n我打算去爬瓦利诺斯的巨树。\n你要是见过它，就会明白这是必要的。

column5: The Grand Tree, hmm...?\nDoes it live up to its namesake?
column6: 巨树，嗯……？\n它配得上这个名字吗？

column5: Yeah, it does!\nIt's probably the ultimate challenge.\nIt overlooks the entire world, you know.
column6: 当然配得上！\n那大概是最极致的挑战。\n你知道，它能俯瞰整个世界。

column5: Interesting. Very interesting.\nPerhaps I should pay Valinorth a visit one day.\nI never thought the mainland could provide me with a challenge.
column6: 有意思。非常有意思。\n也许我该找一天去瓦利诺斯看看。\n我从没想过大陆能给我带来挑战。

column5: Oh, it can! Trust me.\nI've been climbing my entire life.\nWant to hear about more fun places...?
column6: 哦，当然能！相信我。\n我一辈子都在攀爬。\n想听听更多好玩的地方吗……？

column5: I can spare some time, yeah.
column6: 我确实能抽出点时间，好啊。

column5: When I enter the ballroom, I notice my comrades scattered about.{w}\nThey're all enjoying themselves, and having the time of their lives.{w}\nDraycu spared no expense. This was fancier than anything I've ever seen.
column6: 我走进舞厅时，注意到同伴们散落在各处。{w}\n他们都很尽兴，享受着人生中最快乐的时光。{w}\n德雷库不惜血本。这比我见过的任何场面都要奢华。

column5: There's a live band, playing music that's pleasant to the ear.{w}\nCouples sway about on the dance floor, while others feast on a buffet.{w}\nAn open bar attracts many patrons. There's something for everyone here.
column6: 有现场乐队演奏着悦耳的音乐。{w}\n舞池里成双成对的人轻轻摇摆，其他人则在自助餐台前大快朵颐。{w}\n开放式酒吧吸引了许多宾客。这里人人都能找到所爱。

column5: My comrades notice me, and give me smiles as they enjoy the party.{w}\nAs I'm about to step forward, somebody bumps into me from behind.{w}\nIt was clearly on purpose, to grab my attention. I quickly turn around.
column6: 同伴们注意到了我，一边享受宴会一边朝我微笑。{w}\n我正要迈步向前，身后有人撞了我一下。{w}\n那显然是故意的，为了引起我的注意。我迅速转过身。

column5: I hope you're prepared to fight, [firstname].\nYou'll be among the soldiers during tomorrow's fight.\nRegardless of your allegiance, I'm excited to see your abilities.
column6: 我希望你已经准备好战斗了，[firstname]。\n明天的战斗中，你会和士兵们在一起。\n不管你效忠于谁，我都很期待看到你的本事。

column5: I hope you're prepared to fight, [firstname].\nYou'll be among the soldiers during tomorrow's fight.\nHaving your allegiance makes me grateful. We battle together.
column6: 我希望你已经准备好战斗了，[firstname]。\n明天的战斗中，你会和士兵们在一起。\n能得到你的效忠，我很感激。我们并肩作战。

column5: I would be honored to know that you gave it your all.\nEither way, I thought it would be best to come meet you here.\nYou're a guest in my castle. Not a prisoner, as it may have seemed.
column6: 若知道你已拼尽全力，我会感到荣幸。\n无论如何，我觉得最好还是来这里见见你。\n你是我的城堡里的客人，而不是看起来那样的囚犯。

column5: It's just tradition for challenges. They're mostly issued at the castle.\nIt ensures that the people involved in the fight can't back out.\nWe take these battles very seriously, as you could tell.
column6: 这只是挑战的传统。挑战大多都在城堡里发起。\n这能确保参与战斗的人无法退缩。\n如你所见，我们非常看重这种战斗。

column5: I nod. That much was clear.
column6: 我点了点头。这一点显而易见。

column5: I hope we haven't issued any offence.
column6: 我希望我们没有冒犯到你。

column5: I'm glad to hear it. \nThank you for your cooperation.\nWith that said, I have a ball to enjoy.
column6: 听你这么说我很高兴。\n谢谢你的配合。\n话虽如此，我还有舞会要享受。

column5: You're not the first to try and charm your way out of this.\nBacking out of a fight would be abandoning your honor.\nIn Alarinthia, without honor, you have little else to show.
column6: 你不是第一个想靠花言巧语脱身的人。\n临阵退缩就等于抛弃荣誉。\n在阿拉林西亚，没有荣誉，你就几乎一无所有。

column5: With that said, I have a ball to enjoy.\nIf you'll excuse me, I have some subjects to appease.\nHopefully it keeps them happy until next year's party.
column6: 话虽如此，我还有舞会要享受。\n恕我失陪，我还有子民要安抚。\n希望这能让他们开心到明年的宴会。

column5: Prisoners...? At a party this grand?\nIf that's a complaint, you're grasping at straws.\nI have a party to enjoy. I suggest you do the same.
column6: 囚犯……？在这么盛大的宴会上？\n如果这算抱怨，那你可真是抓不住重点。\n我有宴会要享受。建议你也一样。

column5: You accept your fate. That is admirable.\nI wish you best of luck in the future, [firstname].\nIf you'll excuse me, I believe we have a party to enjoy.
column6: 你接受了自己的命运。这令人钦佩。\n祝你好运，[firstname]。\n恕我失陪，我想我们有宴会要享受。

column5: He walks into the ballroom, and is quickly crowded by people.{w}\nGreeting every single one, he ensures that they're all happy.{w}\nHe's very charismatic. Everyone painted him as a savage man.
column6: 他走进舞厅，很快就被人群围住。{w}\n他一一问候每一个人，确保他们都尽兴。{w}\n他极有魅力。所有人都把他描绘成野蛮人。

column5: I notice Damek and Valessa standing off to the side.{w}\nThey don't seem overly interested in joining the party.{w}\nI didn't get their input yet, so maybe I should approach them.
column6: 我注意到达梅克和瓦莱莎站在一旁。{w}\n他们似乎不太有兴趣加入宴会。{w}\n我还没听他们的意见，也许我该过去找他们。

column5: I take a few steps forward, as to not block the entrance of the ballroom.{w}\nThe music gets louder, and the reverberation fills the grand room.{w}\nThe sight and sound combine to make an utterly beautiful experience.
column6: 我向前走了几步，以免挡住舞厅的入口。{w}\n音乐变得更响，回响充满了这间宏伟的大厅。{w}\n景象与声音交织，营造出无比美妙的体验。

column5: I'd try my best to enjoy this before retiring to my private quarters.{w}\nWhen I was ready to sleep, and then fight, that's where I'd go.{w}\nI couldn't delay it forever, but I could occupy myself for a bit.
column6: 我会尽力享受这一切，然后再回我的私人居室。{w}\n等我准备好睡觉、然后是战斗时，我就会去那里。{w}\n我无法永远拖延，但至少能让自己消磨一会儿。

column5: The dance floor is full of people swaying from side to side.{w}\nWatching them celebrate with big smiles helps me relax.{w}\nEven in this awful time, there could still be happiness.
column6: 舞池里满是左右摇摆的人。{w}\n看着他们带着灿烂的笑容庆祝，让我放松下来。{w}\n即便在这样糟糕的时刻，依然能有快乐。

column5: Wow, this place is incredible.\nDraycu sure knows how to throw a party.\nWhat about you, Ulric? Having fun?
column6: 哇，这地方太惊人了。\n德雷库确实很会办宴会。\n你呢，乌尔里克？玩得开心吗？

column5: Draycu is my enemy, Valessa.\nWe're practically being held prisoner.\nDespite that — yeah — I'm having a good time.
column6: 德雷库是我的敌人，瓦莱莎。\n我们实际上就是被当作囚犯扣在这里。\n尽管如此——是啊——我玩得挺开心。

column5: I could tell, actually.\nHow many drinks is that? Five?\nYou don't want to fight with a hangover, do you?
column6: 其实我看得出来。\n那是第几杯了？五杯？\n你不想带着宿醉去战斗吧？

column5: It wouldn't be the first time.\nI've taught myself to fight in any state of being.\nJust something you learn to do when you're as old as I am.
column6: 这又不是第一次了。\n我练就了在任何状态下都能战斗的本事。\n等你到了我这把年纪，自然就学会了。

column5: And how old is that...?
column6: 那到底是多大年纪……？

column5: Old enough. Besides, I doubt I'll have much trouble tomorrow.\nEven if I fought Draycu while drunk, I could take him down.\nSo don't worry about my well being. I've got this.
column6: 够老了。再说，我不觉得明天会有多大麻烦。\n就算喝醉了跟德雷库打，我也能把他撂倒。\n所以别担心我的安危。我应付得来。

column5: You can fight while you're drunk, too...?
column6: 你喝醉了也能战斗……？

column5: Of course. It actually makes things easier.\nYour movements are sloppy, and unpredictable.\nThat's all you need to confuse and overpower your opponent.
column6: 当然。其实那反而让事情更简单。\n你的动作凌乱、难以预测。\n只要这样，就能让对手迷惑并压制他。

column5: Wow, I never thought of it that way.\nThat's a pretty unique fighting style.\nYou'll be sober tomorrow though, right?
column6: 哇，我从没这么想过。\n这真是相当独特的战斗风格。\n不过你明天会清醒的，对吧？

column5: Depends on how tonight goes.\nDon't worry about me, I'll be fine.\nJust go and have a good time, alright?
column6: 那要看今晚过得怎么样。\n别担心我，我会没事的。\n去好好玩吧，好吗？

column5: Alright, if you say so.\nThis is gonna be super interesting.\nTwo undefeated men, locked in combat.
column6: 好吧，既然你这么说。\n这会超级有意思。\n两个未尝败绩的男人，激战一场。

column5: Yeah, I'll make sure to put on a good show for you.\nIt's like a sport. Everybody will be watching intently.\nYou better cheer for me. I'll be listening, Valessa.
column6: 是啊，我一定会为你献上一场好戏。\n这就像一场运动。所有人都会目不转睛地看着。\n你最好为我加油。我会听的，瓦莱莎。

column5: Sure...!
So, Pro, are you having a good time?
column6: 那么，普洛，你玩得开心吗？

column5: Of course. All according to plan.\nI know Ulric is mad, but he'll get over it.\nWe can win this without either of us dying.
column6: 当然。一切都在计划之中。\n我知道乌尔里克很生气，但他会消气的。\n我们可以赢下这一场，谁都不用死。

column5: Yeah, just take out the Leader, right?\nUlric is stubborn though, so be careful.\nI think he might actually try to kill you.
column6: 是啊，只要干掉首领就行了，对吧？\n不过乌尔里克很固执，小心点。\n我觉得他可能真的会试图杀了你。

column5: I've been watching him spar for years.\nI'll be fine — I know exactly how he operates.\nThe best weapon is knowledge, right?
column6: 我看了他练武好多年了。\n我会没事的——我完全清楚他的路数。\n最好的武器就是情报，对吧？

column5: You remembered my lessons!
column6: 你记住我教的东西了！

column5: How could I forget...?\nIt'll help me win this battle. I know it.\nMake sure to cheer me on, alright?
column6: 我怎么会忘……？\n这会帮我赢下这场战斗。我有预感。\n一定要为我加油，好吗？

column5: I think I'd like to remain silent, actually.\nI can't be taking sides at a time like this.\nAs long as we get an alliance, I'm happy.
column6: 其实我想保持沉默。\n这种时候我不能选边站。\n只要能结成同盟，我就满足了。

column5: Oh come on, not even gonna clap for me?\nI'll remember that when you give another speech.
column6: 哦，别这样，连给我鼓个掌都不肯？\n等你下次演讲时我会记住这一点的。

column5: I think my days of giving speeches are over, Pro.\nThat honor belongs to [firstname] now. \nBut I'm sure they'd say the same as me.
column6: 我想我演讲的日子已经结束了，普洛。\n那份荣耀现在属于[firstname]了。\n但我相信他们也会说和我一样的话。

column5: Man, I hate how neutral everybody is acting.\nSometimes it's alright to take a side.
column6: 唉，我真讨厌每个人都摆出一副中立的样子。\n有时候选边站也没什么不好。

column5: Well, it's not that I'm not taking a side.\nIt's more like — I shouldn't gossip to you.\nYou're a combatant, it'd affect your morale.
column6: 嗯，不是我不选边。\n更像是——我不该跟你嚼舌根。\n你是参战者，这会影响你的士气。

column5: What an interesting way to tell me that you side with Ulric.\nSometimes {i}not{/i} saying something, tells me all I need to hear.
column6: 这真是告诉我你站在乌尔里克那边的有趣方式。\n有时候{i}不说{/i}什么，就已经把我要听的都说了。

column5: Now you're just putting words in my mouth.\nThe only person I'd tell is [firstname].
column6: 你这纯粹是在替我乱安话。\n我唯一会告诉的人就是[firstname]。

column5: Interesting.
column6: 有意思。

column5: What...?
column6: 什么……？

column5: You're not the first person to unconditionally trust [firstname].\nPerhaps I could use that to my advantage in the future...
column6: 你不是第一个无条件信任[firstname]的人。\n也许将来我可以利用这一点……

column5: I think this is where I get back to the party.\nThis whole scheming business isn't really for me.\nBut I doubt [firstname] would abuse their role for you.
column6: 我想我该回去参加宴会了。\n这种勾心斗角的勾当实在不适合我。\n但我不认为[firstname]会为你滥用职权。

column5: You're probably right, Damek.\nThey'd have to do it without knowing.\nJust imagine the swindling I could do...!
column6: 你大概说得对，达梅克。\n他们得在不知情的情况下才行。\n想象一下我能骗到些什么……！

column5: Do we know how to throw parties, or what?
column6: 我们是不是很会办宴会，嗯？

column5: Who do you mean, by \"we\"?
column6: 你说的“我们”是指谁？

column5: Our people. Like, the pure ones.\nWe're different civilizations, remember?\nDid The Old Monarchy party like this?
column6: 我们的人。就是那些纯血的人。\n我们是不同的文明，记得吗？\n旧王朝也这样办宴会吗？

column5: This line of questioning is pointless.\nWhy do you wish to know such trivial information?
column6: 这种追问毫无意义。\n你为什么想知道这种琐碎的信息？

column5: It's what friends do, Howl.\nHaven't you ever heard of hanging out...?\nYou just talk to each other, about everything.
column6: 朋友就是这样相处的，豪尔。\n你没听说过“闲聚”吗……？\n就是彼此聊天，什么都聊。

column5: Well, The Old Monarchy {i}did{/i} party.\nAnd to be honest, there isn't much difference.\nDo you see this as a sort of competition?
column6: 嗯，旧王朝{i}确实{/i}也办宴会。\n说实话，区别不大。\n你把这当成一种竞赛吗？

column5: Not exactly. Well, maybe?\nIt's always cool to know you have the most fun.\nDo you not compare yourself to other people...?
column6: 不完全是。嗯，也许吧？\n知道自己玩得最开心总是很爽。\n你从不和别人比较吗……？

column5: That would be a waste of time.\nThere is no benefit in being like other people.\nWe simply wish to be ourselves. Unique.
column6: 那是在浪费时间。\n和别人一样没有任何好处。\n我们只想做自己。独一无二。

column5: See? This is what friends do. They just talk.\nKeep going, Howl. Tell me what's on your mind.\nYou don't need a specific topic, or anything.
column6: 看吧？朋友就是这样。就是聊天。\n继续说，豪尔。告诉我你在想什么。\n你不需要特定的主题，什么都不用。

column5: We would ask why you consider us a friend.\nDoes the world benefit from this conversation?\nIs there a purpose to this sort of interaction?
column6: 我们想问你为什么把我们当作朋友。\n这场对话对世界有好处吗？\n这种交流有什么目的吗？

column5: Perhaps we should talk about the matter at hand.\nThere is much to discuss about Vivien and Draycu.
column6: 也许我们该谈谈眼下的事。\n关于薇薇安和德雷库有很多可说的。

column5: Nope, we can't talk about that.\nThat's {i}work{/i} stuff. We're here to unwind.
column6: 不行，我们不能谈那个。\n那是{i}工作{/i}上的事。我们是来放松的。

column5: Another concept we do not understand.\nEvery moment we waste, the enemy gets stronger.
column6: 又是一个我们无法理解的概念。\n我们浪费的每一刻，敌人都在变强。

column5: It's not a waste, though!\nIf our bond grows stronger, then so do we.\nIt's important to get along with your comrades, Howl.
column6: 可这不是浪费！\n如果我们的羁绊更深，我们也会更强。\n和同伴好好相处很重要，豪尔。

column5: Very well. We will try.\nThis party is an interesting experience.\nAre you having a good time, Fortaime...?
column6: 好吧。我们会试试。\n这场宴会是一次有趣的体验。\n你玩得开心吗，福泰姆……？

column5: There we go! Now you're doing it right.\nJust a few more steps and you'll be ready to dance.
column6: 这就对了！你现在做得很好。\n再练几步，你就能去跳舞了。

column5: We would rather die.
column6: 我们宁愿去死。

column5: While the bodies swayed on the dance floor, Halin and Shane did a dance of their own.{w}\nWeapons clashing, they sparred. It was time for Halin to put his new Apprentice to the test.{w}\nSo far, it seems like their skill was equally matched. A deadlock of the best variety.
column6: 当人群在舞池中摇摆时，哈林和肖恩跳着属于他们自己的舞。{w}\n兵刃相交，他们切磋起来。是时候让哈林考验他的新学徒了。{w}\n到目前为止，两人的技艺似乎不相上下。最精彩的那种僵局。

column5: You put up more of a fight than Sovy ever did.\nWhere did you learn techniques like that, Shane?\nIt almost feels like you're the teacher in this scenario.
column6: 你比索维难对付多了。\n你从哪儿学来那种招式的，肖恩？\n这情景里，几乎像是你在当老师了。

column5: You pick up a lot of stuff on the streets of Mazeo.\nBack when I was younger, it was either fight or die.\nA lot of the Rebels are just like me, so get used to it.
column6: 在马泽奥的街头，你能学到不少东西。\n我年轻的时候，要么打，要么死。\n很多反抗军都跟我一样，所以你习惯就好。

column5: Let me guess, you all banded together after The Occupation.\nThat means if I learn your weaknesses — I learn theirs.\nA weak strategy — all sharing the same fighting style.
column6: 让我猜猜，你们都是在占领之后聚到一起的。\n也就是说，我摸清你的弱点——就等于摸清了他们的。\n很弱的策略——所有人共用同一种战斗风格。

column5: Well now I know why you wanted to spar so soon.\nAnd here I thought you might be warming up to me.
column6: 现在我知道你为什么这么快就想切磋了。\n我还以为你开始对我有好感了呢。

column5: Don't flatter yourself, Shane.
column6: 别自作多情了，肖恩。

column5: Then stop giving me reasons to.
column6: 那就别再给我自作多情的理由。

column5: Their weapons clash again. Halin's sword with Shane's daggers.{w}\nHe had no problem being Halin's match with such small weapons.{w}\nHis agility and quick thinking was more than enough to counter raw strength.
column6: 他们的兵器再次相交。哈林的剑对上肖恩的匕首。{w}\n用这么小的武器与哈林匹敌，他毫不费力。{w}\n他的敏捷与机敏足以抵消纯粹的力量。

column5: I guess Sovy wasn't much of a fighter?
column6: 我猜索维算不上什么战士？

column5: He used to be, but I could tell he always held back.\nThere was doubt in his mind, and it clouded his judgment.\nI trusted it would go away, but you know what happened next.
column6: 他以前是，但我看得出他总是有所保留。\n他心里有疑虑，那蒙蔽了他的判断。\n我以为那会消失，但你也知道后来发生了什么。

column5: Yeah, and he's paying for his mistakes.\nBut you can trust me, Halin. I won't let you down.\nRemember what {i}I{/i} did when we were in Mazeo.
column6: 是啊，他正在为自己的错误付出代价。\n但你可以相信我，哈林。我不会让你失望的。\n记得我们在马泽奥时{i}我{/i}做了什么吗。

column5: You killed your former leader. Your best friend.\nI don't need anything else from you, Shane.\nThat proves your loyalty almost tenfold.
column6: 你杀了你的前首领。你最好的朋友。\n我不需要你再证明什么了，肖恩。\n那几乎十倍地证明了你的忠诚。

column5: Good.
column6: 很好。

column5: Shane sheathes his daggers, done with the sparring.
column6: 肖恩收起匕首，切磋结束了。

column5: So what do you think Sovy will do next?\nI mean, he's no longer welcome in Balteus, right?
column6: 那你觉得索维接下来会做什么？\n我是说，他已经不受巴尔泰乌斯欢迎了，对吧？

column5: I saw him wandering the halls before he left.\nIt's funny. He might actually try to seek out the blade.\nHe was saying something about Alarinthia over and over.
column6: 他离开前我看到他在走廊里游荡。\n说来好笑。他也许真的会去寻找那把剑。\n他一遍又一遍地念叨着阿拉林西亚什么。

column5: What makes him think it'll be in Alarinthia?
column6: 他凭什么觉得那会在阿拉林西亚？

column5: Well, The Rebellion will try its hardest to survive.\nAfter what we did, it makes sense that that'd flee the mainland.\nThey can't come here, so the only other option is Alarinthia.
column6: 嗯，反抗军会竭尽全力求生。\n在我们做了那些事之后，他们逃离大陆是合情合理的。\n他们来不了这里，所以唯一的选择就是阿拉林西亚。

column5: Makes sense when you put it that way.\nMaybe he can regain his honor after all.\nBut I have to ask, why aren't {i}we{/i} going...?
column6: 这么说确实说得通。\n也许他终究能重拾荣誉。\n但我得问一句，为什么{i}我们{/i}不去……？

column5: The Rebellion will come here eventually.\nWe have the home advantage if we sit and wait.\nThere's no way they can overpower our army.
column6: 反抗军迟早会来这里。\n如果我们按兵不动，就拥有主场优势。\n他们绝无可能压过我们的军队。

column5: That's smart.\nSo we're really doing this.\nWe're going to end The Rebellion.
column6: 这很聪明。\n所以我们是认真的。\n我们要终结反抗军。

column5: And any more that may come.\nI sense a bright future for us, Shane.\nAnd we'll do it all — for The Triumvirate.
column6: 还有之后可能出现的任何人。\n我感觉我们前途光明，肖恩。\n而这一切——都是为了三人执政团。

column5: Yeah. For The Triumvirate.
column6: 是啊。为了三人执政团。

column5: I walk over to Damek, as he's standing alone in the corner of the ballroom.{w}\nHe looks a bit awkward, like he knows he doesn't fit in. But I don't blame him.{w}\nWith the story he told me last time, I knew a crowded ballroom floor would frighten him.
column6: 我走向达梅克，他独自站在舞厅的角落。{w}\n他看起来有点局促，像是知道自己格格不入。但我不怪他。{w}\n想起他上次告诉我的故事，我就知道拥挤的舞池会让他害怕。

column5: Hey there, [firstname].\nI hope you're having a good time.\nI mean, given the circumstances, of course.
column6: 嘿，[firstname]。\n希望你玩得开心。\n当然，我是指在这种情况下。

column5: I can imagine it's hard to have fun when you know what's coming.\nActually — forget I said that. I don't want to ruin your experience.\nI'm just airing my own grievances. Forgive my venting.
column6: 我能想象，明知接下来会发生什么，很难玩得开心。\n其实——当我没说。我不想破坏你的兴致。\n我只是在发泄自己的不满。原谅我发牢骚。

column5: I tell him it's fine, and then stand beside him.{w}\nTogether, we watch the patrons dance in the center of the room.{w}\nThey look like they're having the time of their lives, while we just stand here.
column6: 我告诉他没关系，然后站到他身旁。{w}\n我们一起看着宾客们在房间中央起舞。{w}\n他们看起来正享受着人生最快乐的时光，而我们只是站在这里。

column5: You know, I've been thinking.\nI faced death back in Mazeo, and I'll face it tomorrow.\nAfter that, I'll just go on to face it again when we attack Balteus.
column6: 你知道，我一直在想。\n我在马泽奥面对过死亡，明天还要再面对一次。\n之后，等我们攻打巴尔泰乌斯时，我还要再面对一次。

column5: I could die tomorrow, or the next day, or the day after.\nSo I keep asking myself, what should I do before I die?\nA lot comes to mind, but a few are very important to me.
column6: 我可能明天就死，或者后天，或者大后天。\n所以我不断问自己，死之前我该做些什么？\n想到很多，其中有几件对我非常重要。

column5: I want to go back to where it happened, [firstname].\nBack to the place where I spent the last moments with my Mother.\nI've never been back there since I grabbed that pendant. I was scared.
column6: 我想回到事情发生的地方，[firstname]。\n回到我与母亲共度最后时光的地方。\n自从抓起那条吊坠后，我就再没回去过。我害怕。

column5: Just {i}thinking{/i} about that place made it seem like it was happening all over again.\nI can't even imagine what would happen if I went back there for real, you know?\nIt's easy to avoid, since the town square is quite large. But I'm done avoiding things.
column6: 光是{i}想到{/i}那个地方，就仿佛一切又重演了一遍。\n我甚至无法想象如果真的回到那里会怎样，你懂吗？\n要避开很容易，因为镇广场相当大。但我受够逃避了。

column5: I could've died back in those tunnels, [firstname].\nSomething like that really puts things into perspective.\nIf I die — I want to make sure I've lived life to the fullest.
column6: 我在那些隧道里本可能死掉，[firstname]。\n那种事真的会让人重新看待一切。\n如果我死了——我想确保自己已活得淋漓尽致。

column5: So that means there's a few things I'd like to do.\nMost importantly, I'd like to go back to where I lost my Mother.\nI don't want that place to hold power over me. {i}I{/i} want the power.
column6: 所以这意味着有几件事我想去做。\n最重要的是，我想回到我失去母亲的地方。\n我不想让那个地方控制我。{i}我{/i}想要掌握主动权。

column5: You already know about some of my other fears, too.\nBut it'd be ill-mannered of me to request your help for those.\nSo, about Mazeo. I'd just like a good friend to be by my side.
column6: 你也已经知道我其他的一些恐惧了。\n但为那些事求你帮忙，未免太失礼了。\n所以，关于马泽奥。我只希望有个好朋友陪在我身边。

column5: He blushes, and shuffles in place.{w}\nIt was clear that he meant his fear of physical contact.{w}\nI could help him with his Mazeo trip, but I stop to think about the rest.
column6: 他脸红了，脚在原地蹭来蹭去。{w}\n显然他指的是对肢体接触的恐惧。{w}\n马泽奥之行我可以帮他，但我停下来思考其余的事。

column5: Can you say something, Monarch?\nI don't know if I can handle such an awkward silence.
column6: 你能说点什么吗，君主？\n我不知道自己能不能忍受这么尴尬的沉默。

column5: Really...? I can't thank you enough, [firstname].\nI just know that I wouldn't be able to do this myself.\nHaving someone by my side makes me that much stronger.
column6: 真的……？我怎么谢你都不够，[firstname]。\n我知道自己一个人做不到这件事。\n有人陪在身边，让我变得坚强得多。

column5: All of them...? Then that means—\nYou know what, I'll let you take the lead on that one.\nWe're a long way from Mazeo, after all. I can be patient.
column6: 全部……？那也就是说——\n算了，那件事就由你来主导吧。\n毕竟我们离马泽奥还远着呢。我可以耐心等。

column5: Well, then I'll stop trying to fill the gaps so much.\nBut I'd expect a lot of silence if you help me out in Mazeo.\nOnce I go back to that spot, I have no idea how I'll react.
column6: 那好，我就不再那么拼命找话填补冷场了。\n不过如果你在马泽奥帮我，恐怕会有很多沉默。\n一旦回到那个地方，我不知道自己会有什么反应。

column5: He smiles, almost like a weight was lifted from his shoulders.{w}\nIt would be important for him to enter the final battle with a clear mind.{w}\nWhen we got back to the mainland, there was no reason {i}not{/i} to help him.
column6: 他笑了，仿佛肩上的重担被卸下。{w}\n能头脑清明地迎接决战，对他很重要。{w}\n等我们回到大陆，就{i}没有{/i}理由不帮他。

column5: Well, that's pretty much all I had to say.\nI'll let you get back to whatever you were doing.\nUnless there's anything else you had to say before you go?
column6: 嗯，我想说的差不多就是这些了。\n你去忙你的事吧。\n除非你走之前还有什么想说的？

column5: Of course. It was nice to chat with you.\nCome see me when we get back to the mainland.\nHopefully we'll have time for some final errands.
column6: 当然。和你聊天很愉快。\n等我们回到大陆，来找我。\n希望我们还有时间办些最后的琐事。

column5: I'd hate to go right from here to Balteus.\nWe need a final reprieve before we end all of this.\nNo regrets — just in case we don't survive the war.
column6: 我可不想从这里直接就去巴尔泰乌斯。\n在结束这一切之前，我们需要最后的喘息。\n不留遗憾——以防我们没能活过这场战争。

column5: He smiles. It was a grim thought, but a realistic one.{w}\nIf we made it to Balteus, we might not make it back home.{w}\nI'd need to be content with everything I did up until that point.
column6: 他笑了。这想法很沉重，却很现实。{w}\n如果我们到了巴尔泰乌斯，也许就回不了家了。{w}\n到那时，我得对在此之前所做的一切都感到满足。

column5: I leave his side and wander back into the center of the ballroom.{w}\nThe hours were slowly passing by, I couldn't delay tomorrow's battle forever.{w}\nThat thought weighs heavy on my mind as I contemplate what to do next.
column6: 我离开他身旁，踱回舞厅中央。{w}\n时间慢慢流逝，我无法永远拖延明天的战斗。{w}\n我思考接下来该做什么时，这个念头沉沉压在心头。

column5: Oh, really? Did my talk about seizing the day inspire you?\nI mean, I guess I could keep you company. I don't have any other plans.\nAnd just in case it goes badly tomorrow, you deserve a really good night.
column6: 哦，真的？我那番把握当下的话激励到你了吗？\n我是说，我可以陪着你。我也没有别的安排。\n而且万一明天出了岔子，你也该有个美好的夜晚。

column5: He smiles and we walk around the ballroom together.{w}\nWe stop at the buffet table, and inspect our potential options.
column6: 他笑了笑，我们一起在舞厅里走动。{w}\n我们停在自助餐台前，打量有什么可选的。

column5: Alarinthian pastries...? Are these any good?\nIf you're seizing the day, then I guess I should too.
column6: 阿拉林西亚的糕点……？这些好吃吗？\n既然你要把握当下，那我想我也该这样。

column5: He grabs one of them, and starts to eat it.{w}\nAfter a few bites, he starts to cough and his eyes open wide.{w}\nHe wipes away crumbs that fall on his attire, and blushes, embarrased.
column6: 他拿起一块，开始吃起来。{w}\n吃了几口，他咳了起来，眼睛睁得老大。{w}\n他擦掉落在衣服上的碎屑，窘得脸都红了。

column5: Of course they're infused with alcohol. Somehow...\nEverything in this nation has some sort of twist to it.\nYou can never just “get what you want” in Alarinthia.
column6: 果然掺了酒。不知怎么……\n这个国家的一切都带着某种花样。\n在阿拉林西亚，你永远别想“要什么就得到什么”。

column5: Well, unless, of course, I'm talking about {i}you{/i}.\nA fine place to have our first date, despite the circumstances.\nWhen you forget about the coliseum nonsense, this isn't too bad.
column6: 嗯，当然，除非我说的是{i}你{/i}。\n抛开眼下的处境，这倒是个初次约会的好地方。\n只要忘了竞技场那档子事，这里还不算太糟。

column5: If things go well, then maybe we can come back next year.\nPeople do that stuff, right? I mean — celebrate anniversaries?\nWhen you take the throne, you can travel wherever you want.
column6: 如果一切顺利，也许明年我们还能再来。\n人们会这么做的，对吧？我是说——庆祝周年纪念？\n等你登上王位，想去哪儿就能去哪儿。

column5: And I'd be honored if you let me stand by your side.\nYou know, I was always too scared to flirt, or bond with anybody.\nBut I guess a changed perspective is one benefit of a near-death experience.
column6: 如果你让我站在你身边，我会感到荣幸。\n你知道，我以前总是太害怕，不敢跟人调情，也不敢与人亲近。\n但我想，心态的转变大概是濒死体验带来的一个好处。

column5: If you could even call it “near”. I'm pretty sure I {i}did{/i} die.\nAnd you want to know what scared me the most? Nothing happened.\nWhen I was younger, they said I'd see my Mother again in the afterlife.
column6: 如果那还能叫“濒死”的话。我很确定我{i}确实{/i}死了。\n你想知道最让我害怕的是什么吗？什么也没发生。\n我小的时候，他们说我死后就能再见到母亲。

column5: That's kind of what kept me going. That thought made me happy.\nIn fact, I even smiled in my final moments. I'd finally see her again.\nThe world is a cruel place, though — and of course, nothing happened.
column6: 那算是支撑我活下去的念头。那个想法让我感到快乐。\n事实上，我在最后的时刻甚至笑了。我终于能再见到她了。\n可这世界是残酷的——当然，什么也没发生。

column5: Until I opened my eyes again, and saw you and Howl.\nThat changed something inside of me. My priorities shifted.\nThe thought of seeing my Mother again had completely disappeared.
column6: 直到我再次睁开眼，看到了你和豪尔。\n那改变了我内心的某些东西。我的优先次序变了。\n想再见到母亲的念头彻底消失了。

column5: If I chased the future, I'd never enjoy the present.\nThat's part of why I agreed to join you on this date, actually.\nI just wish I was able to realize this sooner. Before the attack.
column6: 如果我追逐未来，就永远无法享受当下。\n其实，这也是我答应陪你共度这次约会的原因之一。\n我只希望自己能早些明白这一点。在那场袭击之前。

column5: The Monarchy saved me by using their power to heal me.\nI'll never waste the second chance they gave me. Never.\nI'll embrace it, and savor every moment — until the end.
column6: 王朝用他们的力量治好我，救了我。\n我绝不会浪费他们给我的第二次机会。绝不。\n我会拥抱它，珍惜每一刻——直到尽头。

column5: We continue chatting, and spending time with one another.{w}\nThe events in the Rebel HQ definitely made him a changed man.{w}\nAnd it was a good change, too — he's “seizing the day”, as it were.
column6: 我们继续闲聊，彼此相伴。{w}\n反抗军总部的事件无疑让他脱胎换骨。{w}\n而且是好的转变——可以说，他正在“把握当下”。

column5: When we returned to Mazeo, I'd take him back to that fateful spot.{w}\nBut with me by his side, I think he'd be able to overcome his past.{w}\nAnd when that happened — we'd build a new, happy future — together.
column6: 等我们回到马泽奥，我会带他回到那个命运攸关的地方。{w}\n但有我在他身边，我想他能克服过去。{w}\n而当那一刻到来——我们会一起构筑崭新而幸福的未来。

column5: Damek's loyalty scene has been unlocked.{w}\nLoyalty scenes will be unlocked at the end of Act Four.{w}\nThey can be initiated from the War Table in the Rebel HQ.
column6: 达梅克的忠诚剧情已解锁。{w}\n忠诚剧情将在第四幕结束时解锁。{w}\n可以在反抗军总部的作战桌上开启。

column5: I approach Valessa, and watch her inspect the buffet table.{w}\nIt looks like she's having a hard time deciding what to eat.{w}\nIt's all free though, so I'd have some of everything.
column6: 我走向瓦莱莎，看着她打量自助餐台。{w}\n她似乎正为难该吃什么。{w}\n反正都是免费的，换我就每样都尝一点。

column5: Why do they need to put alcohol in everything...?\nThese pastries would be fine on their own, you know.\nJust because you can, doesn't mean that you {i}should{/i}.
column6: 他们为什么非得往所有东西里加酒……？\n你知道，这些糕点本身就很好吃。\n能做不代表{i}就该{/i}做。

column5: She fills a plate with a few random sweets.{w}\nIt appears that they're all alcoholic in nature.{w}\nThat sounds fancy, but they're all just doused.
column6: 她随手往盘子里装了几样甜点。{w}\n看来那些本质上都是含酒的。{w}\n听起来很高级，其实不过是浇了酒而已。

column5: The locals are sure eating this stuff up, though.\nCall me old fashioned, but food and drink should stay separate.\nIf this is a delicacy around here, then Alarinthia isn't really my place.
column6: 不过当地人确实吃得津津有味。\n说我老派也好，但食物和酒就该分开。\n如果这算是这里的珍馐，那阿拉林西亚真不是我的归属。

column5: She smiles, as she continues filling her plate.
column6: 她一边继续往盘子里装，一边微笑。

column5: But you gotta eat, right?\nThis isn't the kind of place you want to go hungry.\nI never thought I'd miss some of the food back in Valinorth.
column6: 但总得吃点东西，对吧？\n这种地方可不适合饿着肚子。\n我从没想过自己会怀念瓦利诺斯的一些食物。

column5: But enough about that.\nAre you having a good time, [firstname]?\nAside from the whole coliseum business, of course.
column6: 不过这些就不说了。\n你玩得开心吗，[firstname]？\n当然，竞技场那档子事除外。

column5: That's for sure. Everybody seems so happy.\nIt almost makes you forget where we are.\nI never pictured Alarinthia as “peaceful”.
column6: 那倒是。每个人看上去都那么开心。\n几乎让人忘了我们身在何处。\n我从没把阿拉林西亚想象成“安宁之地”。

column5: Oh stop it, [firstname], you're embarrassing me.\nThere's far more interesting people here than me.\nTry mingling with the locals. I'll {i}always{/i} be around.
column6: 哦，别说了，[firstname]，你让我不好意思了。\n这里比我有趣的人多的是。\n去和当地人交际交际吧。我{i}永远{/i}都在。

column5: I see your quick wit doesn't cave under stress.\nThat's good. We need some more optimism around here.\nIf only that's all it took to win wars, though. We'd be set.
column6: 看来你的机敏在压力下也不会垮。\n这很好。我们这儿需要更多乐观。\n不过要是光靠这个就能打赢战争就好了。那我们早就稳了。

column5: I kind of agree, but it's nice in this castle.\nHe could've thrown us in some prison cells, right?\nI guess we picked the perfect time to come pay him a visit.
column6: 我有点同意，不过这城堡确实不错。\n他本可以把我们丢进牢房，对吧？\n看来我们挑了个绝佳的时机来拜访他。

column5: I guess so. Could be better, could be worse.\nI wonder if your coronation ceremony would've been like this.\nIt's supposed to be the party of a lifetime. I'm sad we had to cancel it.
column6: 我想是吧。可能更好，也可能更糟。\n我在想你的加冕典礼会不会也是这样。\n那本该是一生一次的宴会。可惜我们不得不取消。

column5: She smiles softly while eating the pastries on her plate.{w}\nIt isn't much longer until they're all gone. She must've been starving.{w}\nI don't blame her. The journey here was taxing in every possible way.
column6: 她一边吃盘里的糕点，一边温柔地笑着。{w}\n没过多久就吃光了。她一定是饿坏了。{w}\n我不怪她。这一路的旅程在各方面都耗人心力。

column5: Oh, I forgot to tell you.\nI talked to Alex a little more on the way here.\nYou know, to learn a little bit more about our parents.
column6: 哦，我忘了告诉你。\n来这儿的路上，我又和亚历克斯聊了聊。\n你知道，想多了解一点我们父母的事。

column5: Oh, I forgot to tell you.\nI talked to Nada a little more on the way here.\nYou know, to learn a little bit more about our parents.
column6: 哦，我忘了告诉你。\n来这儿的路上，我又和娜达聊了聊。\n你知道，想多了解一点我们父母的事。

column5: Part of me was hoping to hear something positive.\nYou know, like they were paragons of virtue or something.\nI thought maybe — just maybe — they were good people.
column6: 我内心有一部分希望能听到些正面的东西。\n你知道，比如他们是美德的典范之类的。\n我以为也许——只是也许——他们是好人。

column5: As she talks, the live band starts to play a bit louder.{w}\nPeople flood to the dance floor with their partners.{w}\nValessa watches all of the couples with a wide smile.
column6: 她说话时，现场乐队演奏得更响了些。{w}\n人们带着伴侣涌向舞池。{w}\n瓦莱莎笑眯眯地看着一对对伴侣。

column5: She places her empty plate back on the table.
column6: 她把空盘子放回桌上。

column5: Sorry, the music kind of cut me off.\nRight — I was talking about our parents.\nI learnt so much about them on the trip here.
column6: 抱歉，音乐声把我打断了。\n对——我刚才在说我们父母的事。\n这趟旅程让我了解到他们很多事。

column5: She nods and smiles.
column6: 她点头微笑。

column5: Wait, what...?\n[firstname], I don't know how to dance!\nI'd just end up embarrassing the both of us!
column6: 等等，什么……？\n[firstname]，我不会跳舞！\n我只会让我们俩都丢脸！

column5: I shake my head, and grab her hand.{w}\nSlowly leading her to the dance floor, I take the initiative.{w}\nI tell her that nobody here really knows how to dance. It's just fun.
column6: 我摇摇头，牵起她的手。{w}\n我主动迈出步子，慢慢带她走向舞池。{w}\n我告诉她，这里没人真的会跳舞。只是图个开心。

column5: Fun...? Well don't say I didn't warn you.\nThey'll be teasing us about this for years to come.\nI can endure some teasing for you, though. You're worth it.
column6: 开心……？别说我没警告过你。\n往后好几年他们都会拿这事打趣我们。\n不过为了你，我受得了被人打趣。你值得。

column5: She blushes, and I slowly guide our hands to the right position.{w}\nOne of my hands rests on her back, holding her close to my body.{w}\nThe other grips her hand, and holds it outward, our fingers intertwined.
column6: 她脸红了，我慢慢引导我们摆好手的位置。{w}\n我一只手搭在她背上，把她搂近怀里。{w}\n另一只手握着她的手向外抬起，十指交缠。

column5: We sway side to side, in time with the music, and she laughs, embarrassed.{w}\nAs if to hide her blushing face, she presses her head firmly against my body
column6: 我们随着音乐左右摇摆，她不好意思地笑了。{w}\n仿佛要藏起泛红的脸，她把头紧紧贴在我身上。

column5: I guess this isn't so bad.\nSo you wanted to hear about our parents...?
column6: 我想这也没那么糟。\n所以你想听听我们父母的事……？

column5: I nod, as we continue to dance. I really have no idea what I'm doing.{w}\nLooking at everybody else, I notice they all display the same footwork.{w}\nIt's carefully calculated, so nobody bumps into each other as they dance.
column6: 我点点头，我们继续跳着。其实我完全不知道该怎么做。{w}\n看看其他人，我发现他们脚下都是同样的步法。{w}\n那是精心算计过的，这样跳舞时谁也不会撞到谁。

column5: I mimic that, while I wait for Valessa to speak.
column6: 我一边等瓦莱莎开口，一边照着做。

column5: Just a quick warning, it's not the best atmosphere for this story.\nI mean, talking about Pirates doesn't exactly fill one with joy.\nBut I think it's important to know more about our families.
column6: 先提醒你一句，这故事不太适合在这种气氛里讲。\n我是说，聊海盗可不会让人开心。\n但我觉得多了解自己的家人很重要。

column5: Like I said, I was hoping to hear some good news.\nI always pictured our parents as these perfect, heroic people.\nBut it turns out, they really weren't. They were bad people, [firstname].
column6: 就像我说的，我本希望能听到些好消息。\n我一直把我们的父母想象成完美、英勇的人。\n可事实证明，他们根本不是。他们是坏人，[firstname]。

column5: I know that pirates get involved in shady things, but they embraced it.\nKilling, stealing, smuggling, you name it. They were {i}legends{/i} in Mazeo.\nThey had a whole network operating for them while they were back home.
column6: 我知道海盗会涉足见不得光的勾当，可他们乐在其中。\n杀人、偷盗、走私，什么都干。他们在马泽奥是{i}传奇{/i}。\n他们在家乡时，有一整张关系网为他们运作。

column5: That's how they managed to have a presence in both nations at once.\nThey went to Mazeo every month or so to inspect their operations in person.\nExplains how they managed to raise us, and balance their double lives.
column6: 他们就是这样得以同时在两个国家都留下势力的。\n他们每个月左右去一趟马泽奥，亲自检查他们的生意。\n这也解释了他们怎么能在抚养我们的同时维持双重生活。

column5: We continue to dance, and I listen intently.{w}\nHer grip on my hand becomes tighter, and her body moves closer.{w}\nI can tell she's getting more relaxed, as confidence appears in her movements.
column6: 我们继续跳舞，我专注地听着。{w}\n她握我的手更紧了，身体也靠得更近。{w}\n看得出她越来越放松，动作里透出了自信。

column5: Maybe it's for the best that they passed on when they did...\nThe village, and Salus, raised us. They gave us our sense of morals.\nI can't say I'd be too happy if I inherited the morals of our parents.
column6: 也许他们在那个时候去世反而是好事……\n是村子，还有萨卢斯，把我们养大。是他们给了我们是非观。\n要是继承了父母的品性，我可不敢说自己会高兴。

column5: They could've dragged us into the life of piracy as we grew up, too.\nThat would be dangerous. We could've died years ago, you know?\nIf {i}you{/i} died, then right now, the world would have no hope at all.
column6: 他们也本可能在我们成长的过程中把我们拖进海盗的生活。\n那很危险。我们可能几年前就死了，你知道吗？\n如果{i}你{/i}死了，那如今这世界就一点希望都没有了。

column5: So maybe The Occupation was meant to happen.\nIt's guided us to where we are now — shaped us into who we've become.\nIf we let {i}them{/i} shape us, then I have no idea where we'd be right now.
column6: 所以也许占领是注定要发生的。\n它把我们引到如今的境地——把我们塑造成现在的样子。\n如果我们任由{i}他们{/i}塑造，那我不知道我们现在会在哪里。

column5: It's so weird, since children usually aspire to be like their parents.\nBut right now, I'm using them as a roadmap on what {i}not{/i} to do.\nAll I can do, is dedicate my life to being better people than them.
column6: 这很奇怪，因为孩子通常都渴望成为父母那样的人。\n但现在，我把他们当作一张“{i}不要{/i}这么做”的路线图。\n我唯一能做的，就是把一生献给成为比他们更好的人。

column5: Maybe that can undo some of the damage they've done.\nBecause I know they tore families apart. They killed, and robbed.\nSome would say that in the end, being murdered was their justice.
column6: 也许这样能弥补一些他们造成的伤害。\n因为我知道他们拆散过家庭。他们杀人，也抢劫。\n有人会说，最后被人杀死就是他们的报应。

column5: But I don't think death is a good form of justice.\nThey should've gotten the chance to make up for their crimes.\nWith them gone, I feel like it's our job to do what they couldn't.
column6: 但我不认为死亡是伸张正义的好方式。\n他们本该有机会弥补自己的罪行。\n既然他们不在了，我觉得替他们做那些做不到的事，就是我们的责任。

column5: So that's something else I'm going to fight for.\nI'll make up for the damage our parents inflicted.\nI'll give the world peace, so no one has to feel pain.
column6: 所以这也是我要为之奋斗的另一件事。\n我会弥补我们父母造成的伤害。\n我会给这个世界带来和平，让谁都不必再感受痛苦。

column5: We'll make a world that doesn't {i}need{/i} people like our parents.\nA world that treats everyone with unconditional love, and equality.\nNo one will have to live in poverty, or turn to a life of crime.
column6: 我们要造出一个{i}不需要{/i}我们父母那种人的世界。\n一个以无条件的爱与平等对待所有人的世界。\n没有人需要活在贫困中，也没有人需要走上犯罪的道路。

column5: Nobody deserves to be a victim of circumstance.\nTo have their life determined by the world around them.\nNo, that's not it at all. {i}We{/i} shape the world, not the other way around.
column6: 没人活该成为环境的牺牲品。\n没人活该被周遭的世界决定自己的一生。\n不，根本不是那样。是{i}我们{/i}塑造世界，而不是反过来。

column5: She pulls her head back, and looks up in my eyes as we sway.
column6: 她抬起头，在摇摆中望进我的眼睛。

column5: She looks in my eyes, with overwhelming determination.
column6: 她看着我，眼中满是不可动摇的决心。

column5: So let's shape it into something beautiful.\nA place where no one has to resort to being evil.\nI'm sure our parents were introduced to it somehow.
column6: 所以让我们把它塑造成美好的东西吧。\n一个没人需要走向邪恶的地方。\n我相信我们的父母当年也是被引上那条路的。

column5: It's not like they woke up one day just wanting to be pirates.\nMaybe it was their parents before them, or some close friends.\nI guess it doesn't matter, does it? We'll make the cycle end with {i}us{/i}.
column6: 他们又不是某天醒来就突然想当海盗。\n也许是他们的父母，或者某些密友。\n我想那不重要，对吧？我们要让这个循环终结在{i}我们{/i}身上。

column5: And we'll start a new cycle.\nOne of peace, happiness, and prosperity.\nOne where our children can live full, happy lives.
column6: 然后我们会开启新的循环。\n一个和平、幸福、繁荣的循环。\n一个让我们的孩子能过上充实快乐人生的循环。

column5: I smile at her, and dip her low as the music comes to an end.{w}\nI hold that pose for as long as I can, enjoying the sense of togetherness.{w}\nShortly after, I raise her back up, and we leave the dance floor amongst the crowd.
column6: 我朝她微笑，在音乐结束时将她低低地放倒。{w}\n我尽可能久地保持着那个姿势，享受这份相依的感觉。{w}\n不久后，我扶她起身，我们随着人群离开了舞池。

column5: The music slowly comes to an end, and everybody leaves the dance floor.{w}\nValessa watches for a while before speaking again, enjoying the moment.
column6: 音乐缓缓结束，所有人都离开了舞池。{w}\n瓦莱莎享受了一会儿这一刻，才再次开口。

column5: When we get back to Mazeo, I want to see their old hideout.\nAnd I'd really like it if you came with me, [firstname].\nIt'll give me a sense of closure, and let me move on.
column6: 等我们回到马泽奥，我想去看看他们以前的藏身处。\n我真的很希望你能陪我去，[firstname]。\n那会让我有个了结，好继续往前走。

column5: I never thought I'd learn more about our parents on this journey.\nAnd I'm even more surprised that it's a truth I never expected.\nBut if I could go back, and never learn it? Well, I wouldn't.
column6: 我从没想过会在这趟旅程中了解更多父母的事。\n更让我意外的是，那是我完全没料到的真相。\n但如果能回到过去，让我永远不知道？嗯，我不会的。

column5: It gives me the drive to become a better person.\nAnd it really makes me appreciate everything I have.\nIncluding you, [firstname]. I could never do this alone.
column6: 它给了我成为更好的人的动力。\n也让我真心珍惜自己所拥有的一切。\n包括你，[firstname]。我一个人绝对做不到。

column5: She grabs both of my hands, and looks deep into my eyes.
column6: 她握住我的双手，深深望进我的眼睛。

column5: Thank you for asking me to dance, by the way.\nI guess Draycu's grand ball is a good spot for a first date.\nBut maybe next time, we can go somewhere with better food.
column6: 顺便说一句，谢谢你邀请我跳舞。\n我想德雷库的盛大舞会倒是个初次约会的好地方。\n不过下次，也许我们可以去个食物更好的地方。

column5: She smiles and then runs off, doing her own thing.{w}\nI'm sure almost everybody saw us dance. There was no hiding it.{w}\nBut I'm glad that we did. I want to be with her, no matter the circumstances.
column6: 她笑了笑，然后跑开去忙自己的事了。{w}\n我敢说几乎所有人都看到我们跳舞了。根本藏不住。{w}\n但我很高兴我们跳了。无论如何，我都想和她在一起。

column5: She smiles, and then examines the room.
column6: 她笑了笑，然后环视房间。

column5: I'll let you go and tend to some business, [firstname].\nI should probably talk to Fortaime about this stuff, too.\nHe deserves to know about his parents just as much as us.
column6: 我放你去处理些事务吧，[firstname]。\n我也该跟福泰姆聊聊这些事。\n他和我们一样有权知道自己父母的事。

column5: I nod, and watch her as she slowly walks away.{w}\nOnly {i}she{/i} could turn a horrible truth into such contagious optimism.{w}\nBut she was right. We'd create a better world, where no one had to be hurt.
column6: 我点点头，看着她慢慢走开。{w}\n只有{i}她{/i}能把一个骇人的真相变成如此有感染力的乐观。{w}\n但她说得对。我们会创造出一个更好的世界，一个谁都不必受伤的世界。

column5: Valessa's loyalty scene has been unlocked.{w}\nIt will be available after the completion of Act Four.{w}\nLoyalty scenes can be initiated from the Rebel HQ War Table.
column6: 瓦莱莎的忠诚剧情已解锁。{w}\n它将在第四幕完成后开放。{w}\n忠诚剧情可以从反抗军总部的作战桌开启。

column5: As soon as I get to my private quarters, I rest the blade beside the bed.{w}\nIt feels good to get that weight off my shoulders. Too bad the relief would be ephemeral.{w}\nI sit down in the bed, and think about what would be coming in the next few days.
column6: 一到我的私人居室，我就把剑靠在床边。{w}\n卸下那份重担的感觉真好。可惜这份轻松转瞬即逝。{w}\n我在床上坐下，想着接下来几天会发生什么。

column5: A tournament to decide the fate of Alarinthia. An alliance to help us attack Balteus.{w}\nNot even a day or two after the coliseum battle, we'd be sailing into the final battle.{w}\nWould we win...? Or would we perish? The blade showed me nothing when I asked.
column6: 一场决定阿拉林西亚命运的锦标赛。一个帮我们攻打巴尔泰乌斯的同盟。{w}\n竞技场之战后不到一两天，我们就要启航奔赴决战。{w}\n我们会赢吗……？还是会灭亡？我问那把剑时，它什么也没显示。

column5: I sit down on the bed, and decide not to try using the blade again.{w}\nThe anxiety of not being able to know almost wasn't worth it.{w}\nIt was supposed to do what I wanted. Was I not strong enough?
column6: 我在床上坐下，决定不再尝试使用那把剑。{w}\n无法得知答案的焦虑几乎让人难以承受。{w}\n它本该如我所愿。是我不够强吗？

column5: The blade was so mysterious, I'd probably never know.{w}\nI lie down, having had enough of today's events. Things were crazy.{w}\nJust when I think we get to relax, we're pushed into more conflict.
column6: 那把剑太神秘了，我大概永远也不会明白。{w}\n我躺下，今天的事已经够多了。一切都疯狂得很。{w}\n每当我以为能松口气，我们又被推入新的冲突。

column5: But this conflict has clearly proven divisive among our team.{w}\nPro and Ulric against each other? Vivien and Draycu, too.{w}\nPerhaps this is a lesson that casualties are unavoidable.
column6: 但这场冲突显然在我们队里造成了分裂。{w}\n普洛和乌尔里克互相对立？薇薇安和德雷库也是。{w}\n也许这是给我们的一课：伤亡无法避免。

column5: I close my eyes, and hold onto a firm resolve in my heart.{w}\nNo. None of my comrades would die tomorrow. They'd survive.{w}\nWe were all survivors, and that's what we'd continue to do. Forever.
column6: 我闭上眼，心中抱定坚定的决心。{w}\n不。我的同伴们明天谁都不会死。他们都会活下来。{w}\n我们都是幸存者，而且我们会一直如此。永远。

column5: Instead of falling asleep, however, I find myself someplace familiar.{w}\nIt's the same locale I found myself in after falling asleep in Peregrino.{w}\nThis wasn't just some random dream. I had to be here for a purpose.
column6: 然而，我并未入睡，而是发现自己来到一个熟悉的地方。{w}\n这和我当初在佩雷格里诺入睡后抵达的地方一样。{w}\n这绝不是随机的梦。我来这里一定有目的。

column5: All I knew is that this was The Triumvirate's chambers.{w}\nThere was no doubt in my mind. But why was I here...?{w}\nNot only once, but twice? There needed to be a reason.
column6: 我只知道这里是三人执政团的议事厅。{w}\n我心中毫无怀疑。可我为什么会在这里……？{w}\n不止一次，而是两次？一定有原因。

column5: The blade weighs heavy on my back, and I slowly pull it out.{w}\nI can sense that it's pulsating with energy — reacting to something.{w}\nI notice the idol at the back of their chambers. That's what it was.
column6: 背上的剑沉甸甸的，我缓缓将它拔出。{w}\n我能感觉到它涌动着能量——正在对什么作出反应。{w}\n我注意到他们议事厅后方的那尊灵像。原来就是它。

column5: But why was the blade reacting to something like that...?{w}\nIt doesn't look like any spirit idol I've ever seen. What is it...?{w}\nI feel a strong pull. Almost like I have no choice but to approach it.
column6: 可那把剑为什么会对那种东西有反应……？{w}\n它不像我见过的任何灵像。那到底是什么……？{w}\n我感到一股强烈的牵引。几乎像是别无选择，只能靠近它。

column5: I take slow, heavy steps toward the idol, and I feel eyes upon me.{w}\nNot just one or two pairs. It's almost like all of Alestia is watching me.{w}\nI can sense my comrades at my back, almost as if they're encouraging me.
column6: 我朝灵像迈出缓慢而沉重的步子，感觉有目光落在我身上。{w}\n不止一两双。几乎像是整个阿莱斯蒂亚都在注视着我。{w}\n我能感觉到同伴们就在我身后，仿佛在鼓励我。

column5: It helps me push forward, as I feel resistance emanate from the idol.{w}\nWhy would I feel such a strong pull to something that doesn't want me...?{w}\nI push through, in spite of that resistance, and continue to act instinctually.
column6: 这助我向前，尽管我感觉到灵像散发出的抗拒。{w}\n为什么我会对不想接纳我的东西感到如此强烈的牵引……？{w}\n不顾那份抗拒，我硬撑过去，继续凭本能行动。

column5: Yes. Fulfill your purpose. \nDo what you were meant to do.
column6: 好。履行你的使命。\n做你注定要做的事。

column5: That's The Triumvirate's voice.{w}\nI remember it from last time I was here.{w}\nBut I have no idea what they mean by my \"purpose\".
column6: 那是三人执政团的声音。{w}\n上次来这里时我就记得。{w}\n但我完全不明白他们说的“使命”是什么意思。

column5: Still, I can't deny my instinct, and I keep pressing forward.{w}\nIt isn't much longer before I'm standing in front of the idol.{w}\nIt radiates pure malice, and pure evil. It fills me with fright.
column6: 但我无法否认自己的本能，继续向前。{w}\n没过多久，我就站在了灵像前。{w}\n它散发着纯粹的恶意与纯粹的邪恶。让我满心恐惧。

column5: I look down at my blade. Was I meant to destroy this...?{w}\nI'm confused as to why I'm doing what The Triumvirate tells me to.{w}\nIt's that conflict that causes this \"dream\" to end, and jolt me awake.
column6: 我低头看着自己的剑。我是注定要毁掉它吗……？{w}\n我困惑于自己为何要照三人执政团的吩咐去做。{w}\n正是这份矛盾，让这场“梦”结束，把我猛地惊醒。

column5: I rise up in fright, gripping my chest, and panting heavily.{w}\nI look over at the blade resting on my bedside. What happened...?{w}\nIt feels as if no time passed at all, but it's already the next morning.
column6: 我惊恐地坐起，捂着胸口，大口喘气。{w}\n我望向靠在床边的剑。发生了什么……？{w}\n感觉像一点时间都没过去，可已经是第二天早晨。

column5: Just what I needed. No rest before a massive battle.{w}\nThe fates were playing cruel tricks on me during this journey.{w}\nBut I had to keep going. I couldn't give in. It would be over soon.
column6: 真是我需要的。大战前一点休息都没有。{w}\n这趟旅程中，命运一直在残酷地戏弄我。{w}\n但我必须继续走。我不能屈服。很快就结束了。

column5: I stand up, and strap the blade to my back.{w}\nAs if on a cue, I hear a knock at the door, before it's opened.{w}\nDraycu steps in, not seeming to care if I was receptive of him.
column6: 我起身，把剑绑到背上。{w}\n仿佛掐准了时机，我听到敲门声，接着门就被推开了。{w}\n德雷库走进来，似乎并不在意我是否愿意见他。

column5: It's your turn, [firstname].
column6: 轮到你了，[firstname]。

column5: My turn...?
column6: 轮到我了……？

column5: We're transporting you to the coliseum one by one.\nThat way, you're less inclined to try and escape us.\nYou'll be the last one, so it's almost time to fight.
column6: 我们正把你们一个一个送往竞技场。\n这样你们就不太会想从我们手里逃跑。\n你是最后一个，所以差不多该开打了。

column5: I nod. It all makes sense.
column6: 我点了点头。全都说得通。

column5: I'd advise not wasting much time.\nBut head to the coliseum when you're ready.\nYou'll be followed by myself and a few guards.
column6: 我建议你别浪费太多时间。\n但准备好之后就去竞技场吧。\n我和几名卫兵会跟着你。

column5: Oh, and good luck. You'll need it.\nThe entire nation will be watching, and cheering.\nBut whether it's for your victory, or demise, remains to be seen.
column6: 哦，还有，祝你好运。你会需要的。\n整个国家都会看着，为你欢呼。\n但是为你的胜利还是为你的死亡，还不好说。

column5: He rests his back against the wall, and crosses his arms.{w}\nThis is really happening. A battle to decide the nation's fate.{w}\nI guess I'd head to the coliseum when I was ready to fight.
column6: 他背靠墙壁，双臂交叉。{w}\n这一切真的在发生。一场决定国家命运的战斗。{w}\n我想等我准备好战斗时，就去竞技场。

column5: Heat pours in through the windows, and makes it almost unbearable.{w}\nIt wasn't too bad last night, but now it's morning, and I can feel the extreme heat.{w}\nI'm glad that we won't be in this nation for much longer. I could never handle it.
column6: 热气透过窗户灌进来，几乎让人无法忍受。{w}\n昨晚还不算太糟，但现在是早晨，我能感受到那种酷热。{w}\n很高兴我们不会在这个国家待太久了。我可永远受不了这地方。

column5: These look comfortable, but unfortunately, I have no time to waste.{w}\nI need to get to the coliseum as soon as possible for the tournament.{w}
column6: 这些看起来很舒服，可惜我没时间可浪费。{w}\n我得尽快赶到竞技场参加锦标赛。{w}

column5: I'd go back to bed if it weren't so hot in this room.{w}\nOh, and I guess we also have a tournament to fight in.
column6: 要不是这房间这么热，我就回去睡了。{w}\n哦，还有，我想我们还有场锦标赛要打。

column5: It's a book about leadership-deciding coliseum battles.
column6: 那是一本关于决定领袖归属的竞技场战斗的书。

column5: A book rests on the nightstand.{w}\nIt appears to be about coliseum battles.{w}\nNot regular ones, though. The leadership ones.
column6: 床头柜上放着一本书。{w}\n看起来是关于竞技场战斗的。{w}\n不过不是普通的战斗。是决定领袖归属的那种。

column5: The kind of battle I'd be fighting in today.{w}\nI wonder if it was placed here on purpose.{w}\nWe did play into Draycu's hand, after all.
column6: 正是我今天要参加的那种战斗。{w}\n我在想这是不是故意放在这里的。{w}\n毕竟我们确实是中了德雷库的算计。

column5: I make my way to the coliseum alongside Draycu and some of his soldiers.{w}\nIt's a massive, towering structure, almost putting the castle to shame.{w}\nIt makes sense that it'd be bigger. Alarinthia was all about fighting.
column6: 我和德雷库以及他的一些士兵一起前往竞技场。{w}\n那是一座庞大高耸的建筑，几乎让城堡都相形见绌。{w}\n它更宏伟也说得通。阿拉林西亚的一切都与战斗有关。

column5: Well, here we are.\nIf you head on inside, you'll find your allies.\nAfter that, you'll all be escorted to a private room.
column6: 好了，我们到了。\n你进去就会找到你的同伴。\n之后，你们都会被带到一间私人房间。

column5: You'll have a few moments to prepare once you're in there.\nBut I'd say within the next hour or two, the battle will be over.\nThey don't last very long if both sides have prepared enough.
column6: 进去之后，你们会有片刻时间做准备。\n但我说，接下来一两个小时内，战斗就会结束。\n如果双方都准备充分，这种战斗不会持续太久。

column5: He crosses his arms, looks at me dismissively.
column6: 他双臂交叉，轻蔑地看着我。

column5: You may wonder why I'm doing this even though you sided against me.\nThe answer to that is, it's in my nature to show my enemy some kindness.\nI do not kill in cold blood. I will mourn you, and honor your memory, [firstname].
column6: 你也许想知道，既然你站在我的对立面，我为何还要这么做。\n答案是，向敌人施予善意是我的天性。\n我不会冷血地杀人。我会哀悼你，并尊崇你的记忆，[firstname]。

column5: It is a noble thing, to die for your beliefs.\nPerhaps your memory will inspire future generations.\nGenerations that can go on to be killed, just like you.
column6: 为自己的信念而死，是高尚的。\n也许你的记忆会激励后世的人。\n那些后人，也会像你一样被杀死。

column5: He steps forward, looking me dead in the eye.
column6: 他上前一步，直勾勾地盯着我的眼睛。

column5: I do not expect to lose to Vivien.\nI've killed far stronger men than him.\nSome would call you foolish for your choice.
column6: 我不认为自己会输给薇薇安。\n我杀过比他强得多的人。\n有人会说你的选择很愚蠢。

column5: With a smile, he lets out a soft laugh.
column6: 他微微一笑，轻声笑了出来。

column5: But I am not one of those people.\nAs I said, I treat my enemies with kindness.\nYou may have realized it, but that's why I held the ball.
column6: 但我不是那种人。\n就像我说的，我以善意对待敌人。\n你也许已经明白了，这正是我举办舞会的原因。

column5: But the ball is over, so I must find another way to be kind.\nAnd that is showing you a swift, painless end in the coliseum.\nYou wish to die for your beliefs. It would be my honor to aid you.
column6: 但舞会结束了，所以我必须另寻方式表达善意。\n那就是在竞技场给你一个迅速、无痛的结局。\n你愿为信念而死。能助你如愿，是我的荣幸。

column5: After saying these harsh words, he enters the coliseum.{w}\nI have no choice but to follow him, as the guards block any avenue of escape.{w}\nThere was no way we'd lose. We have Ulric on our side. He's a match for Draycu.
column6: 说完这些刻薄的话，他走进了竞技场。{w}\n卫兵封住了所有退路，我别无选择，只能跟上。{w}\n我们绝不可能会输。我们有乌尔里克。他能与德雷库匹敌。

column5: I must thank you again for offering me your allegiance, [firstname].\nUlric may seem strong, but we will win this battle — I know it.\nI could do it blindfolded. I've bested stronger men than him.
column6: 我必须再次感谢你向我效忠，[firstname]。\n乌尔里克看似很强，但我们会赢下这场战斗——我知道。\n我蒙着眼都能做到。我击败过比他更强的人。

column5: We must make sure that we show them kindness, however.\nThey wish to die for their cause, so we are granting them a gift.\nDo not kill in cold blood. You must mourn them, and never forget.
column6: 不过，我们必须确保对他们施以善意。\n他们愿为自己的事业而死，所以我们是在赐予他们礼物。\n不要冷血地杀戮。你必须哀悼他们，永远不忘。

column5: These battles are not senseless killing. There is honor in them.\nVivien may think of us barbaric, but that is far from the truth.\nWe only want our nation to be in the hands of the strong.
column6: 这些战斗不是无谓的杀戮。其中自有荣誉。\n薇薇安也许觉得我们野蛮，但那与事实相去甚远。\n我们只是希望国家掌握在强者手中。

column5: Perhaps that is why The Triumvirate has not subjugated us yet.\nIf this nation became like the mainland, I couldn't say the same.\nIdeals only get you so far. Strength must guide you from there.
column6: 也许这就是三人执政团至今未能征服我们的原因。\n如果这个国家变得像大陆一样，我就不敢这么说了。\n理想只能带你走到一定程度。之后必须靠力量引领。

column5: He smiles at me, a look of confidence on his face.
column6: 他朝我微笑，脸上是自信的神情。

column5: And it is strength that we have.\nI'll see you inside, [firstname].
column6: 而我们拥有力量。\n里面见，[firstname]。

column5: He enters the coliseum after saying those words.{w}\nI have no choice but to follow him, as the guards block any avenue of escape.{w}\nThere was no way we'd lose. Draycu was undefeated. We'd earn his allegiance.
column6: 说完那些话，他走进了竞技场。{w}\n卫兵封住了所有退路，我别无选择，只能跟上。{w}\n我们绝不可能会输。德雷库未尝败绩。我们会赢得他的效忠。

column5: The coliseum towers above me. It must fit thousands of spectators.{w}\nFrom everything I've heard, every seat would be full when we started.{w}\nI'm filled with anxiety and fright. Could I really perform under such scrutiny?
column6: 竞技场高耸在我面前。它一定能容纳数千名观众。{w}\n据我听到的一切，开战时每个座位都会坐满。{w}\n我满心焦虑与恐惧。我真的能在如此众目睽睽之下发挥好吗？

column5: Sovy looks on at the ocean, watching the ripples and waves.{w}\nHe remains silent, attracting the suspicion of the Captain.{w}\nApproaching Sovy, he attempts to converse to pass the time.
column6: 索维望着大海，看着泛起的涟漪与波浪。{w}\n他保持沉默，引起了船长的疑心。{w}\n船长走向索维，想聊聊天打发时间。

column5: It shouldn't be longer than a few more hours.\nBut I have to ask — what brings you to Alarinthia?
column6: 应该不会超过几个钟头了。\n但我得问一句——你去阿拉林西亚做什么？

column5: It's probably better for you not to know.\nI don't want to involve people in my problems.
column6: 你不知道大概对你更好。\n我不想把别人卷进我的麻烦里。

column5: Involve away. What else are we going to do...?\nYou paid me tenfold to take {i}you{/i}, and you alone.\nHow can you expect me not to question that?
column6: 卷进来吧。我们还能做什么……？\n你付了我十倍的价钱，只载{i}你{/i}一个人。\n你怎么能指望我不起疑？

column5: I expect you to do the job you're paid for.\nAnything else is unnecessary, don't you agree?
column6: 我指望你做你拿了钱该做的事。\n其他都是多余的，你不觉得吗？

column5: Look. The way I see it, we're friends here.\nIf you need a ferryman back, I'd love to help you out.\nTreat me with the cold shoulder, and you could get stranded.
column6: 听着。在我看来，我们算是朋友。\n如果你回来时还需要摆渡人，我很乐意帮忙。\n要是你对我冷冰冰的，你可能会被困在那边。

column5: Is that a threat...?
column6: 那是在威胁我吗……？

column5: Of course not. I'm just curious.\nHere, let's start with the basics.\nWhat kind of work do you do...?
column6: 当然不是。我只是好奇。\n这样吧，我们从最基础的开始。\n你是做什么工作的……？

column5: You already know what I do for a living.\nDon't you think I deserve to know — as a courtesy?\nI don't care if you're breaking the law, or anything like that.
column6: 你已经知道我是靠什么谋生的。\n你不觉得作为礼尚往来，我也该知道吗？\n就算你在违法什么的，我也不在乎。

column5: No, I'm not breaking the law.\nBut honestly, I don't know how to answer your question.\nI guess you could say that I'm “between things” right now.
column6: 不，我没违法。\n但老实说，我不知道该怎么回答你。\n大概可以说，我现在“处于空档期”。

column5: And why is that...?
column6: 那是为什么呢……？

column5: I thought it was time to seek out better opportunities.
column6: 我觉得是时候去找更好的机会了。

column5: In Alarinthia...?
column6: 去阿拉林西亚……？

column5: To be honest, I have no idea.\nI just know some people who might be there.\nTalking to them should get things on the right track.
column6: 老实说，我也不知道。\n我只是认识一些可能在那里的人。\n跟他们谈谈，应该能让事情走上正轨。

column5: And what line of work are you in?
column6: 那你是干哪一行的？

column5: I guess you could say I seek out information.\nNothing pleases me greater than learning the truth.\nBut the people I worked for were far less than honest.
column6: 你可以说我是找情报的。\n没什么比得知真相更让我满足。\n但我效力的那些人却远谈不上诚实。

column5: Lied to by your bosses? Join the club.\nThey'll do anything to save face and get their way.\nThat's part of why I work on my own, now. I get you.
column6: 被上司骗了？欢迎加入。\n为了保全面子和达成目的，他们什么都干得出来。\n这也是我现在单干的原因之一。我懂你。

column5: The Captain scoffs, surprised at Sovy's earlier hesitance.
column6: 船长嗤笑一声，对索维先前的犹豫感到意外。

column5: Is that what you were so worried to open up about?\nTrust me, almost everybody knows what that's like.\nI hope your next opportunity is more fruitful.
column6: 你之前那么不敢开口，就是因为这个？\n相信我，几乎人人都懂那种滋味。\n希望你的下一个机会更有收获。

column5: I can only hope.
column6: 我只能这么希望。

column5: So what did they lie to you about?
column6: 那他们对你撒了什么谎？

column5: Everything.
column6: 一切。

column5: Then I can see why you'd run away.
column6: 那我能理解你为什么逃走了。

column5: Excuse me...?
column6: 你说什么……？

column5: I just mean — it's totally understandable.
column6: 我只是说——这完全可以理解。

column5: Sovy steps toward the Captain clenching his fists.{w}\nHe brings himself face to face, as if trying to intimidate.
column6: 索维握紧拳头，朝船长迈步上前。{w}\n他凑到对方脸前，像是想威慑他。

column5: I'm not running away. I'm doing what's right.
column6: 我不是在逃。我在做正确的事。

column5: The Captain matches his gaze, taking one step forward.{w}\nHe didn't give in to Sovy's intimidation. He was an even match.
column6: 船长迎上他的目光，向前迈了一步。{w}\n他没有被索维的威吓压服。两人势均力敌。

column5: Sometimes running away {i}is{/i} the right thing to do.
column6: 有时候逃跑{i}确实{/i}是正确的选择。

column5: They stare at each other, until Sovy backs away.{w}\nSomething was different. Normally, he would stand his ground.{w}\nBut he no longer served The Triumvirate. He had nothing to prove.
column6: 他们对视着，直到索维退开。{w}\n有什么不一样了。换作平时，他会寸步不让。{w}\n但他已不再为三人执政团效力。他没什么需要证明的了。

column5: I'm sorry, you're right.\nI didn't mean to start something on your boat.\nOnce we get to Alarinthia, you'll never see me again.
column6: 抱歉，你说得对。\n我不是有意在你的船上惹事。\n等我们到了阿拉林西亚，你就再也见不到我了。

column5: There's no need to go that far.\nDon't misunderstand me. I've got your back.\nYou're not the only man who's run away, you know.
column6: 没必要说到那种地步。\n别误解我。我是站你这边的。\n你知道，你不是唯一一个逃过的人。

column5: Why else do you think I live at sea?\nSometimes I don't set foot on land for {i}weeks{/i} at a time.\nI prefer to be out here, where I live on my own terms. I'm free.
column6: 你以为我为什么住在海上？\n有时候我一连{i}好几周{/i}都不踏上陆地。\n我更喜欢待在这里，按自己的方式生活。我是自由的。

column5: Free, hmm...?
column6: 自由，嗯……？

column5: Yeah, there's no better way to live.\nImagine not being shackled by higher-ups.\nYou're fully capable of making your own decisions.
column6: 是啊，没有比这更好的活法了。\n想象一下不受上级束缚。\n你完全可以自己做决定。

column5: Sovy sighs, and looks down at the ground.{w}\nIt was his own decision that got him into this mess to begin with.{w}\nBut even though The Triumvirate wasn't pleased, he stood by his actions.
column6: 索维叹了口气，低头看着地面。{w}\n一开始把他拖进这摊麻烦的，正是他自己的决定。{w}\n尽管三人执政团并不满意，他仍坚持自己的作为。

column5: That would be wonderful...\nI've been a subordinate for my entire life.\nI think it's finally time that I carved my own path.
column6: 那会很好……\n我这辈子一直是个下属。\n我想是时候开辟属于自己的路了。

column5: I enter the coliseum, and quickly scan the area for my friends.{w}\nA massive flame burns in the center of the room, making the heat even worse.{w}\nI wonder why they'd do something like that. This place confuses me sometimes.
column6: 我走进竞技场，迅速扫视四周寻找我的朋友。{w}\n房间中央燃着巨大的火焰，让热气更加难耐。{w}\n我在想他们为什么要这么做。这地方有时真让我费解。

column5: Draycu is nowhere to be seen. Perhaps he's already in the private room.
column6: 德雷库不见踪影。也许他已经进了私人房间。

column5: I notice Valessa, Fortaime, and Howl standing far away from the flame.{w}\nNo sign of anybody else though. I decide to approach them and ask what's up.{w}\nThey turn to me and smile, while Howl shows the face of complete indifference.
column6: 我注意到瓦莱莎、福泰姆和豪尔站在离火焰很远的地方。{w}\n却不见其他人的踪影。我决定走过去问问情况。{w}\n他们转向我微笑，而豪尔则是一脸完全的漠然。

column5: I can't believe how cool this place is.\nToo bad I can't actually enjoy it. I'm super stressed.\nI'm really worried that we might lose somebody today.
column6: 真不敢相信这地方这么酷。\n可惜我根本没法享受。我紧张死了。\n我真的很担心我们今天会失去某个人。

column5: Have we actually worked out who's fighting?\nI mean, which of our members are joining Draycu's reserve forces?\nThe Leader and the Champion, we know. But what about everyone else?
column6: 我们真的确定谁上场了吗？\n我是说，我们有那些人要加入德雷库的后备队？\n首领和斗士，这我们知道。但其他人呢？

column5: Howl steps forward.
column6: 豪尔上前一步。

column5: Ulric fights with Vivien. Pro fights with Draycu.\nVivien's reserve forces are part of his own army.\nDraycu's reserve forces will borrow from our army.
column6: 乌尔里克对战薇薇安。普洛对战德雷库。\n薇薇安的后备队来自他自己的军队。\n德雷库的后备队则会从我们的军队里借调。

column5: We believe using the Monarch Vessels would be the best idea.\nWe wouldn't want to put any more of our main forces at risk.\nIf we win, our allegiance will make this sacrifice worthwhile.
column6: 我们认为使用君主容器是最好的办法。\n我们不想再让主力部队涉险。\n如果我们赢了，我们的效忠会让这份牺牲变得值得。

column5: We believe using our Created Seers will be the best idea.\nWe wouldn't want to put any of our main members at risk.\nIf we win, our allegiance will make this sacrifice worthwhile.
column6: 我们认为使用我们的人造先知是最好的办法。\n我们不想让任何核心成员涉险。\n如果我们赢了，我们的效忠会让这份牺牲变得值得。

column5: It is unfortunate that we will have to kill our own.\nBut we cannot change what Pro has set in motion.\nAll we can do is try to focus on taking Draycu's life.
column6: 我们不得不杀死自己人，这很不幸。\n但我们无法改变普洛已经启动的事。\n我们唯一能做的，就是集中精力取德雷库的性命。

column5: This will also give Draycu's side an incredible boost in strength.\nWe will need every advantage possible if we want to win this battle.\nBut we should avoid killing our own. Focus on Vivien's life, [firstname].
column6: 这也会让德雷库一方的力量大幅增强。\n如果我们想赢下这场战斗，就需要尽可能多的优势。\n但我们应该避免杀死自己人。把目标放在薇薇安的性命上，[firstname]。

column5: He looks at me.
column6: 他看着我。

column5: As for Valessa's question, [firstname] will fight among Vivien's reserve forces.\nIt is important for a leader to fight for their beliefs. No delegation at times like this.\nThis means that several of our key members will be put in harm's way.
column6: 至于瓦莱莎的问题，[firstname]将在薇薇安的后备队中作战。\n领袖为自己的信念而战很重要。这种时候不能推给别人。\n这意味着我们的几位核心成员将身陷险境。

column5: As for Valessa's question, [firstname] will fight among Draycu's reserve forces.\nIt is important for a leader to fight for their beliefs. No delegation at times like this.\nThis means that several of our key members will be put in harm's way.
column6: 至于瓦莱莎的问题，[firstname]将在德雷库的后备队中作战。\n领袖为自己的信念而战很重要。这种时候不能推给别人。\n这意味着我们的几位核心成员将身陷险境。

column5: It may be impossible for us to avoid the loss of our reserve forces.\nBut we may be able to win without losing any of our comrades.\nWe must simply focus on the lives of Vivien and Draycu.
column6: 我们也许无法避免后备队的损失。\n但也许我们能不折损任何同伴就取胜。\n我们只需把目标集中在薇薇安和德雷库的性命上。

column5: He crosses his arms, speaking sternly.{w}\nIt was more of a demand, than a request.
column6: 他双臂交叉，语气严厉地开口。{w}\n那与其说是请求，不如说是命令。

column5: Do your best to kill Draycu before any harm can come to Pro or Ulric.\nWe have the option to mitigate our losses, so we must take it.
column6: 尽力在普洛或乌尔里克受到伤害之前杀掉德雷库。\n我们有办法减轻损失，所以必须这么做。

column5: Do your best to kill Vivien before any harm can come to Pro or Ulric.\nWe have the option to mitigate our losses, so we must take it.
column6: 尽力在普洛或乌尔里克受到伤害之前杀掉薇薇安。\n我们有办法减轻损失，所以必须这么做。

column5: No pressure, or anything like that.
column6: 完全没有压力，绝对没有。

column5: So you'll be safe, Howl?\nAlong with myself and Fortaime?\nWhat about Damek? He ran off with Pro and Ulric.
column6: 那你会安全喽，豪尔？\n还有我和福泰姆？\n那达梅克呢？他跟普洛和乌尔里克跑走了。

column5: I suppose we'll find out.\nWe should head to the private room and prepare.\nThe battle will be starting in a matter of minutes.
column6: 我想我们很快就会知道。\n我们该去私人房间准备了。\n战斗几分钟后就要开始。

column5: Damek ran off with both of the Champions? That's odd.{w}\nI guess they've been close friends for a long time, though.{w}\nPerhaps he just wants a chance to say goodbye to them.
column6: 达梅克跟两位斗士都跑走了？真奇怪。{w}\n不过我想他们已经是多年的挚友了。{w}\n也许他只是想找个机会跟他们道别。

column5: The odds of survival for everybody involved were less than stellar.{w}\nBut there was nothing we could do. Everything was put into place.
column6: 所有涉事者的生还几率都不算高。{w}\n但我们无能为力。一切都已安排妥当。

column5: Let's go ask him ourselves, [firstname].\nThis whole ordeal is kind of confusing.\nFor a while, I was scared I'd have to fight.
column6: 我们自己去找他问问吧，[firstname]。\n这整件事有点让人摸不着头脑。\n有一阵子我还怕自己得上场打。

column5: Yeah, same — and I was really worried.\nBut now I feel bad that I'm just going to watch.\nThis whole situation is so messed up.
column6: 是啊，我也是——我当时真担心。\n但现在只做个旁观者，又让我心里不好受。\n整个局面真是糟透了。

column5: It is less than ideal, yes.\nBut we cannot change our circumstances.\nLet us gather together for last minute preparations.
column6: 确实不尽如人意。\n但我们无法改变处境。\n让我们聚到一起做最后的准备吧。

column5: Only by preparing for the coming storm, can we avoid tragedy.\nIf we stand here any longer, the odds of losing our comrades will grow.\nDo not let the enemy get the upper hand. That has happened enough.
column6: 唯有为即将到来的风暴做好准备，我们才能避免悲剧。\n如果我们再站在这里，失去同伴的几率只会增加。\n别让敌人占上风。这种事已经发生太多次了。

column5: He points to a nearby staircase. That must lead to the private room.{w}\nYeah, everything was happening so fast. I could use a few moments to plan.{w}\nOne last team huddle before the fight would help. We need to minimize our losses.
column6: 他指向附近的楼梯。那一定通往私人房间。{w}\n是啊，一切都发生得太快了。我需要一点时间谋划。{w}\n战前来最后一次团队商讨会有帮助。我们得把损失降到最低。

column5: We need to make it through this without losing Pro, or Ulric.{w}\nIf such a thing is even possible, then we'll find out how to do it.{w}\nAnd if its not...? Well, I honestly don't know what I'd do.
column6: 我们必须挺过这一关，不能失去普洛或乌尔里克。{w}\n如果这真有可能，那我们就找出办法。{w}\n如果真的不可能……？嗯，老实说我也不知道自己会怎么办。

column5: Hey, Valessa?
column6: 嘿，瓦莱莎？

column5: Yeah? What's up?
column6: 嗯？怎么了？

column5: I saw you dancing with [firstname]...
column6: 我看见你和[firstname]跳舞了……

column5: And...?
column6: 然后呢……？

column5: Are you two a thing now?
column6: 你们俩现在是一对了吗？

column5: Does it matter...?
column6: 这重要吗……？

column5: No, I was just curious! Really!\nAs you know, we're already dating.\nI just figured it'd be my business, too.
column6: 不，我只是好奇！真的！\n你知道，我们已经在交往了。\n我只是觉得这也算我的事。

column5: Well then, I guess we are.\nIt was all so \"in the moment\".\nI guess we can work out specifics later?
column6: 那好吧，我想是的。\n一切都那么“当下即兴”。\n细节我们以后再谈，好吗？

column5: Sounds good to me!\nThis is pretty awesome, isn't it?\nNothing can tear the three of us apart...!
column6: 我没意见！\n这挺棒的吧？\n没什么能把我们三个人分开……！

column5: Yeah, I guess you're right.\nNo matter what, we're always together.\nValinorth, Mazeo, Alarinthia, and soon enough, Balteus...
column6: 是啊，我想你说得对。\n不管怎样，我们永远在一起。\n瓦利诺斯、马泽奥、阿拉林西亚，很快还有巴尔泰乌斯……

column5: Oh yeah — the final attack...\nI just hope we all survive it, don't you?\nI'd hate to get close to you both, and then lose you.
column6: 哦对——最后的进攻……\n我只希望我们都能活下来，你不也是吗？\n我可不想刚和你们俩亲近起来，就失去你们。

column5: Well I have no intentions of dying, Fortaime.\nI'm just worried about [firstname], though. \nThe stress that this quest is bringing {i}me{/i} is unreal.
column6: 我可没打算死，福泰姆。\n我只是担心[firstname]。\n这趟任务带给{i}我{/i}的压力简直难以置信。

column5: I can't even imagine being the one in charge.\nTo rule this world after the war is over...?\nHopefully I can help make it easier.
column6: 我甚至无法想象身为掌权者会是什么样。\n战争结束后要统治这个世界……？\n希望我能帮忙让它轻松一些。

column5: Yeah, same! That's my main goal in all of this.\nWe're all a team, so we need to help each other out.\nI'll have your back as long as you have mine, Valessa.
column6: 是啊，我也是！这就是我做这一切的主要目标。\n我们是一个团队，所以要互相扶持。\n只要你挺我，我就挺你，瓦莱莎。

column5: Of course, and then we can both protect [firstname].\nWe'll all be looking out for each other. Totally unstoppable.\nI can picture The Triumvirate quaking in their boots right now.
column6: 当然，然后我们就能一起保护[firstname]。\n我们都会彼此照应。完全无可阻挡。\n我现在就能想象三人执政团吓得发抖的样子。

column5: Heh, yeah. We'll take them down no problem.\nSo what do you say...? Together until the end?
column6: 嘿，是啊。我们会轻松把他们拿下。\n那你意下如何……？一起走到最后？

column5: Until the end.
column6: 走到最后。

column5: Well, I was just curious!\nIt seemed pretty passionate from what I saw.\nThink you're gonna rule at [firstname]'s side?
column6: 嗯，我只是好奇！\n从我看到的来说，那可挺热烈的。\n你觉得你会和[firstname]并肩统治吗？

column5: I didn't even think of that, to be honest.\nBut we all worked together in Valinorth, right?\nNo matter what happens, I'm sure we'll make it work.
column6: 老实说，我都没想过这个。\n但我们在瓦利诺斯时就是一起共事的，对吧？\n不管发生什么，我相信我们都能处理好。

column5: Of course, my queen.
column6: 当然，我的女王。

column5: Whoa, hold on. {i}Please{/i} don't call me that.
column6: 哇，等等。{i}拜托{/i}别这么叫我。

column5: Yes, your highness.
column6: 遵命，殿下。

column5: Fortaime...!
column6: 福泰姆……！

column5: Oh, lighten up — I'm just messing around.\nI know you'd make a fine ruler. You're awesome.
column6: 哦，放松点——我只是开个玩笑。\n我知道你会是个出色的统治者。你太棒了。

column5: Really...?
column6: 真的……？

column5: Of course...! And it's a real possibility too.\nDating [firstname]...? Do the math, Valessa.
column6: 当然……！而且这真很有可能。\n和[firstname]在交往……？你自己算算，瓦莱莎。

column5: Hmm...
It's not {i}that{/i} complicated.\nEvery King needs a Queen, right?\nI think you fit the bill perfectly. Don't you?
column6: 没那么{i}复杂{/i}。\n每个国王都需要一个王后，对吧？\n我觉得你完全符合条件。你不觉得吗？

column5: Although I guess having two Queens could be complicated.\nMaybe you'd need to have a separate title, but that changes nothing.\nI still think that you fit the bill of ruler perfectly. Don't you agree with me?
column6: 不过我想有两个王后可能也挺麻烦。\n也许你得另有个头衔，但那不影响什么。\n我还是觉得你完全符合统治者的条件。你同意我的看法吗？

column5: I can't answer that question.\nIt would be pretty self serving, wouldn't it?
column6: 我回答不了这个问题。\n那样未免太自夸了，不是吗？

column5: A Queen has no need to be humble, Valessa.\nDrink fancy tea, wear beautiful dresses — do it all!\nI just hope you don't forget about me when you're famous.
column6: 王后不需要谦虚，瓦莱莎。\n喝精致的茶，穿美丽的裙子——全都做一遍！\n我只希望你出名之后别忘了我。

column5: Fortaime, I'd never forget about you.\nAt the very least, you'd make sure of that...\nBut we'd definitely need a royal advisor, right?
column6: 福泰姆，我绝不会忘了你。\n至少你肯定会确保这一点……\n但我们肯定需要一个王室顾问，对吧？

column5: Are you suggesting what I think you're suggesting?
column6: 你是在暗示我以为你在暗示的事吗？

column5: Well, we all worked together back in Valinorth.\nI don't see why it would be any different after the war.\nImagine the three of us being rulers of the entire world.
column6: 嗯，我们当初在瓦利诺斯就是一起共事的。\n我不认为战后会有什么不同。\n想象一下我们三个统治整个世界。

column5: Awesome!
column6: 太棒了！

column5: This party banter is due to your relationship with Valessa.
column6: 这段宴会闲谈是因为你与瓦莱莎的关系而触发的。
